title: Tim Berners-Lee and the First Web Browser (1990)
explainer: In 1989 Tim Berners-Lee proposed a system of linked hypertext documents while working at CERN, and by late 1990 he had built WorldWideWeb, the first web browser and editor, running on a NeXT computer. What began as a way for physicists to share documents became the platform underneath every browser-based app in this track. Seeing how recent and contingent that origin is helps explain why the web still carries design choices from one researcher's early prototype.

title: The iPhone (2007) and the Birth of the App Store Model (2008)
explainer: Apple's iPhone, unveiled in January 2007, initially shipped with no way for outside developers to install native software; Apple only opened the App Store in mid-2008 after developer pressure for first-class access to the hardware. That decision established the 'install a native app from a curated store' model that Android and other mobile platforms soon followed, and it's a large part of why native mobile development looks so different from writing for the open web. Knowing this history clarifies why mobile platforms are more gatekept, and more capability-rich, than the browser.
